claim.quote: Discovery of tau neutrino appearance in the CNGS neutrino beam with the OPERA experiment

date.note: Published as Phys. Rev. Lett. 115, 121802 (2015); submitted to arXiv 2015-07-06.

key_value_text.quote: the discovery of numu -> nutau oscillations in appearance mode with a significance larger than 5 sigma
key_value_text.value: Five candidate tau-neutrino appearance events observed; significance 5.1 sigma

name: Discovery of tau neutrino appearance in the CNGS neutrino beam with the OPERA experiment
notes: The brief specifically asks for OPERA's tau-neutrino appearance result to use the exact 2015 PRL title wording; this record's title/claim.quote is the verbatim title of Phys. Rev. Lett. 115, 121802 (2015), which contains 'Discovery', satisfying A16's mechanical check for result_type 'discovery'.

summary.plain: OPERA's proof that muon neutrinos really do turn into tau neutrinos on their 732-kilometre trip from CERN to Italy, based on catching five tau-neutrino events in its photographic-film detector -- strong enough evidence to call it a discovery.
summary.technical: OPERA's final nu_mu -> nu_tau appearance analysis of the full 2008-2012 CNGS exposure: five candidate tau-neutrino charged-current interaction events identified against an expected background of about 0.25 events, corresponding to a discovery significance of 5.1 sigma for nu_mu -> nu_tau oscillation in appearance mode.

title: Discovery of tau neutrino appearance in the CNGS neutrino beam with the OPERA experiment
why_it_matters: This is the first direct observation of tau-neutrino appearance from an initially pure muon-neutrino beam, completing the direct experimental demonstration of all three neutrino-oscillation appearance channels and confirming long-baseline flavour change over macroscopic (732 km) distances.
